method.screening_detail: All 591 titles were inspected. All 591 complete source bodies were machine-screened for US names/aliases, institutions, policy/legislation/electoral terms, and worldwide/conditional predicates; source matches were classified by their target, not by presence of government vocabulary alone. Full bodies for boundary families, title/criteria discrepancies, named-person targets, FDA/EPA decisions, NASA/EIA measurements, and positive/negative acceptance examples were manually inspected. This is not a claim of sentence-by-sentence manual review of every repeated body.
method.topic_rule: Hold numerical questions involving US politicians/parties/policy/legislation/political entities, including explicit compound and conditional predicates. Specific US federal regulatory decisions are held under the parent campaign disposition. Non-US politics and government-associated scientific/business/technical measurements are not blanket excluded.
method.global_rule: Worldwide existential predicates with no identified US actor or US policy target remain source-eligible. A generic any-country/any-candidate quantifier alone is not treated as an explicit US target. NATO-wide policy and Article 5 collective-defense commitments receive the explicit dispositions recorded below.
method.conditional_rule: An explicit held US political predicate remains held if it is an antecedent or one clause of a compound, even when the other target concerns business, science, or non-US politics.
method.past_event_rule: A completed past US election falling within an old source window is not used to authorize a new numerical political answer.
method.independence_limit: Source targets and quotations were independently inspected; campaign boundary decisions communicated by the parent are identified as decisions, not treated as independent evidence that the source contains additional words. The parent-supplied account of Musk’s political role was not independently researched in this source-only review.

Will the United States pass a federal law regulating the ethical use of artificial intelligence in energy management before January 1, 2028?

Resolution criteria: This question will be resolved as 'Yes' if, between October 1, 2024, and January 1, 2028, the United States passes a federal law specifically aimed at regulating the ethical use of artificial intelligence in energy management. acceptance_examples.reason: Held: directly predicts whether the United States passes a federal AI energy-management law; non-election wording is not grounds for admission.

Will the United States implement a nationwide carbon tax before January 1, 2028?

Resolution criteria: This question will be resolved as 'Yes' if the United States implements a nationwide carbon tax between October 1, 2024, and January 1, 2028. acceptance_examples.reason: Held: explicitly US nationwide carbon-tax law.
